target_customer: Individuals, mostly men, trying to quit pornography, plus spouses, therapists and churches via supporter versions; consumers pay an annual subscription
problem: People who want to quit porn struggle in isolation and shame, and blockers or monitoring tools do not address the underlying emotional drivers. Relay matches users into small private anonymous peer teams for daily accountability.
business_model: Consumer subscription, 149 dollars per year with a 7 day trial and money back guarantee
product_category: Digital peer support app for behavioral recovery

founders.name: Chandler Rogers
founders.background_notes: Has said he struggled with pornography himself. YC page says he led product at two other startups.

founders.name: Jace Kendrick
education: Brigham Young University, Computer Science and Business
founders.background_notes: Web and mobile engineer at Apple per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile app with group matching, check ins, notifications and an SOS alert. Standard engineering for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Matching and content are copyable, though trusted group relationships and church and therapist channels add some stickiness. No hard technical barrier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent was found copying or buying the peer team model. Accountability software incumbents such as Covenant Eyes focus on monitoring.

market_need_then: Pornography use was widely reported as a source of relationship and mental health harm, especially in faith communities in Utah. Founders cited personal experience and BYU startup competition wins in 2021 as early signals of demand.

branding.name_origin: The app was first named Tribe to convey working together and not being alone, then renamed Relay by early 2021. No source explains why Relay was chosen.
branding.domain_note: Uses joinrelay.app, not relay.com, and shares its name with several unrelated products including the workflow tool Relay.app.

identity.visual_style: Warm lifestyle photos of smiling people at home and outdoors
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, hopeful and direct, with short dramatic lines such as your problem is not porn, it is pain, and a faith friendly undertone

branding.brand_signature: The framing that the problem is pain not porn
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by BYU Universe, Utah Business, KSL and LDS podcasts, and the app markets to churches and bishops. No evidence of merch or memes.

brand_strength.rationale: Local and faith community press and a clear message, but a generic name shared by many products and no iconic asset found.

outcome_analysis: Relay is a small bootstrapped style consumer subscription business led by a founder with lived experience, with community distribution through churches and therapists. It remains active and no shutdown, sale or layoffs were found. Funding beyond the YC deal is not publicly confirmed, so its trajectory cannot be judged from rounds, and its claimed outcome numbers are self reported.
notes: CB Insights alone lists a 500K convertible note in September 2022 with Y Combinator; no second source, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. A 2022 Utah Business article said the team had operated without institutional funding. YC lists founding as 2022 but a March 2021 BYU article already describes the app, so founded_year is 2021. Competitor list left empty because all comparison sources found are dated 2024 to 2026; Covenant Eyes, Brainbuddy and Fortify existed as alternatives. Relay.app is an unrelated company.
